items.title: Tranched yield, power perps, tokenized stocks and new launchpads led what shipped this week.
items.summary:
Tranched yield, power perps, tokenized stocks and new launchpads led what shipped this week.

Here are 8 crypto apps worth testing this week 🧠👇

1. @mezzanine_fi: Mezzanine splits one DeFi strategy into a junior and a senior vault, so you pick your risk. Its first vault, the @HastraFi Optimizer, loops yield from auto loans and US home equity loans across Morpho and Kamino. It hit $4.81M TVL in its first 24h, with senior at ~18% and junior at ~38% APY (variable).

Junior absorbs losses first, and the yield comes from private credit, so borrower risk is real.

2. @tradeparagon: Paragon lists 24/7 perps on @HyperliquidX for stocks, Treasury yields and pre-IPO names like Anthropic. This week it unveiled Power Perps, starting with HYPE²: if HYPE doubles, the index quadruples, with no strikes and no expiry.

Longs usually pay funding for that convexity, so HYPE can rise and you can still lose. Check that HYPE² is tradeable in the app before sizing in.

3. @eqxlabs: EQX issues tokenized spot US stocks and ETFs on Hyperliquid, from SPY and QQQ to NVDA and SpaceX, each backed 1:1 by shares held at StoneX, Clear Street and Alpaca. It adds no issuer fees on top of Hyperliquid's trading fee, and with equity perp funding spiking, you can hold the spot token and short the perp to collect it.

4. @miranetwork: Sterling is an OpenAI-compatible inference API that only routes your request to providers Mira has tested, so the Claude, GPT or Gemini you pay for is the model that actually answers. Top up in USDC or $MIRA and pay as you go. The launch post passed 200k views.

5. @priors_trade: Credit lines for AI agents on Robinhood Chain. Agents borrow USDG, pay other agents for work straight from the line, and every repayment lands on a public record backers can read before extending more. 98 new agents joined last week, and 177 repaid a loan in a single 24h stretch.

Backers carry the default risk, so only back what you can afford to lose.

6. @saplingdotcash: Sapling is the first Zcash-native launchpad and trading terminal for Solana coins. You launch and trade straight from your Zcash wallet, and holders get paid in ZEC from trading fees. In its first 41 days it did $45.75M in volume across 531K+ trades, with 10,529 holders and $643.6K in protocol revenue, 90% of which went back to the community.

Most of what launches here is memecoins, and only about 6% of coins graduate, so size small.

7. @floatdotxyz: Float is a new Solana launchpad, powered by @Raydium, for coins paired with stock tokens like NVIDIA, Tesla or McDonald's, or with plain SOL or USDC. It passed $1M in fees within weeks of launch, airdropped $127.5K USDC to its top 100 traders, and has burned about 10% of the $FLOAT supply through buybacks.

It's memecoin territory, and the team is still changing the launch rules every few days, so keep size small.

8. @longdotxyz: LONG is a Robinhood Chain launchpad for coins paired with stock tokens. Since Nov 6, you can launch new stock-token pairs straight from the @RobinhoodCrypto wallet app, with gas covered. Its AI Nexus basket (long AI names, short QQQ) now lets holders vote on what's in it every 7 days and earn a share of its trading fees.

DYOR/NFA.

Anything we should test this week?

items.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence | Center for Security and Emerging Technology
items.summary:
November 9, 2026

The United States leads the world in frontier AI models and computing, but China is pursuing broader paths toward artificial general intelligence, including robotics, “embodiment,” and brain-inspired systems. A forthcoming CSET study compares the two countries’ strengths and asks what U.S. policymakers may miss when they treat AI competition as a single race.

## Executive Summary [...] Do not mistake today’s model rankings for a permanent strategic verdict. The paths to artificial general intelligence and superintelligence remain uncertain. China’s relative weakness in frontier compute coexists with strengths in engineering, deployment, and alternative research approaches. [...] The United States has a substantial lead in the computing resources and models driving today’s AI boom. Yet measuring the competition with China solely by the performance of large language models (LLMs) risks overlooking how China understands the goal and intends to reach it.

Our forthcoming CSET report argues that the two countries pursue different conceptions of artificial general intelligence (AGI).

At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.
